subtitle: Lesson 20 · Scaling & Reliability

code:
Synchronous:
  client -> request -> [wait...] -> response
  connection held open the ENTIRE time

Asynchronous, with a queue:
  client -> request -> job ID returned NOW
  worker picks it up when free; client polls later
caption: A slow AI request holding a connection open doesn't scale the way a fast one does.

code:
Autoscaling alone:
  burst arrives -> need MORE instances RIGHT NOW

Queue in front of autoscaling:
  burst arrives -> requests wait briefly
  -> autoscaling has time to catch up
  -> no request REJECTED, just delayed
caption: Turns "react instantly" into "catch up eventually" -- which matters given slow GPU cold starts.

code:
Normal:   job -> queue -> worker -> succeeds
Failing:  job -> queue -> worker -> FAILS
          -> retried a few times -> still fails
          -> moved to DEAD-LETTER QUEUE, set aside
caption: One poison-pill request shouldn't consume retries and worker time forever.
